transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started with the weekly investment review for the finance-system replacement. We've got a proposed $12 million implementation budget, which fits within the board-approved capital-plan envelope, and the vendor's schedule runs April through December. Before I make the final budget sign-off, I'd like to hear from each of you on the project conditions. Who wants to kick us off?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before we proceed, I want to flag something important from an accounting perspective. I confirmed in a memo received this morning that exactly 60% of the $12,000,000 project cost — that is, $7,200,000 — meets our capitalization criteria. The remaining $4,800,000 would need to be expensed as incurred. I should note that this memo has not yet been circulated to FP&A, so this may be new information for the team.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before Maya makes the final sign-off, I need to flag a critical cash-flow constraint from my forecast review this week. Only $9,000,000 can be funded before the end of the current fiscal year while preserving our approved minimum cash floor. The remaining $3,000,000 must be funded after October 1. This forecast note has not yet been added to the investment packet, so I want to make sure it's on the record before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag something from the procurement side. Yesterday I received the vendor's countersigned commercial schedule, which includes a 20% holdback on each implementation invoice until final acceptance. I should also note that I have not yet uploaded this schedule to the procurement repository, so this may not be reflected in the documentation Maya has seen so far.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Ensure the capitalization memo confirming $7.2M capitalized and $4.8M expensed is formally circulated to FP&A and added to the investment packet.
Add the cash-flow constraint note ($9M current fiscal year, $3M post-October 1) to the investment packet for the record.
Upload the vendor's countersigned commercial schedule, including the 20% holdback provision, to the procurement repository.
Structure the funding plan so no more than $9M is deployed before fiscal year-end, with the remaining $3M scheduled after October 1 to preserve the minimum cash floor.
Track the 20% holdback on each implementation invoice through to final acceptance and ensure holdback releases are reconciled against milestone completion.
